newsitem.title: USA: U.S. appoints top farm trade negotiator.
newsitem.headline: U.S. appoints top farm trade negotiator.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on Tuesday formally announced the nomination of Peter Scher as the United States' chief agricultural trade negotiator.
The creation of the new position of Special Trade Ambassador for Agriculture would increase attention on an "ever-increasing" number of farm trade issues, Barshefsky said in a statement.
A key priority for Scher, whose nomination must be approved by the Senate, will be persuading China to drop barriers to U.S. agricultural goods, Barshefsky said.
Agricultural trade issues are a major factor in talks on China's accession to the World Trade Organisation. They are also an issue in Chile's accession to the North American Free Trade Agreement.

Other farm trade negotiations the United States is currently pursuing include the question of meat inspection equivalency with the European Union, an EU ban on hormone-raised U.S. beef, and imports of Canadian wheat.
"Peter Scher will bring a strong combination of talent and experience to meet a series of critical challenges in opening international markets to our agricultural products," Barshefsky said.
Scher, who served as chief of staff to former Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor, also drew praise from Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman and U.S. farm groups.
"He will be a very valuable leader in the administration's efforts to promote agricultural trade around the world and fight unfair trade restrictions," Glickman said.
The National Cattlemen's Beef Association, the main producer group, said the appointment was a sign the administration recognised the importance of farm trade by elevating it to ambassador status.
